result.topic_en: Gauss looks for spherical right triangles whose sides and angles all have rational sines and cosines. He reduces this to finding pairs of integers a,b and a',b' with ab(b−a)(b+a) and a'b'(b'−a')(b'+a') in the ratio of two squares, tabulates such pairs, and connects them to the pentagon whose ten diagonals are 90°.

Setzt man $P = 90^\circ + 2\varphi - 2\varphi'$
$Q = 2\varphi + 2\varphi'$
so wird
$\operatorname{tg}\tfrac12 p = \sqrt{\frac{\operatorname{tg}2\varphi}{\operatorname{tg}2\varphi'}}$
$\operatorname{tg}\tfrac12 q = \sqrt{\operatorname{tg}2\varphi\cdot\operatorname{tg}2\varphi'}$
$\operatorname{tg}\tfrac12 r = \sqrt{\frac{\sin 4\varphi}{\sin 4\varphi'}}$
also wenn man macht
$a = u\cos\varphi$
$b = u\sin\varphi$
$a' = u'\cos\varphi'$
$b' = u'\sin\varphi'$
$4kmm = u^4\sin 4\varphi$
$4km'm' = u'^4\sin 4\varphi'$

$\operatorname{tg}\tfrac12 r = \frac{m(a'a'+b'b')}{m'(aa+bb)}$ = [-...-]
$\operatorname{tg}\tfrac12 p = \frac{m'ab}{ma'b'} = \frac{m(a'a'-b'b')}{m'(aa-bb)} = \frac{ab(a'a'-b'b')}{kmm'}$
$\operatorname{tg}\tfrac12 q = \frac{2aba'b'}{kmm'} = \frac{2m'ab}{m(a'a'-b'b')} = \frac{2ma'b'}{m'(aa-bb)}$
$\operatorname{tg}\tfrac12(90^\circ-P) = \frac{ab'-ba'}{aa'+bb'}$   $\operatorname{tg}\tfrac12 Q = \frac{ab'+ba'}{aa'-bb'}$
